newsitem.title: USA: Poll finds Rep. Kennedy popularity slipping - poll.
newsitem.headline: Poll finds Rep. Kennedy popularity slipping - poll.

text.p: Controversy surrounding the annulment of his first marriage is tarnishing Representative Joe Kennedy's popularity among Massachusetts voters, according to a poll in Thursday's Boston Herald.
Kennedy, who is preparing for a 1998 gubernatorial run, has found his overall favourability rating slipping to 49 percent, down from 66 percent last fall, the newspaper said.
Of the 355 likely voters surveyed between April 21 and April 23, 38 percent said they had heard a lot about the annulment controversy and said they viewed the Democrat less favourably.

The poll comes at a critical juncture for the congressman. His first wife, Sheila Rauch Kennedy, is launching a national tour promoting her new book, "Shattered Faith," which portrays him as hot-tempered and impatient.
Sheila Rauch Kennedy fought the annulment of the marriage, which was granted in October by Boston church officials. She is now appealing it to the Vatican.
The poll shows Democrat Kennedy trailing incumbent Republican Gov. William Weld 56-35 percent in a prospective 1998 matchup. Weld is considering running for a third term as governor.
